fields.text: Player B says it's not the case that at least 0 of A and F are spies, which is always true since 0≥0, so B lies, thus knave. Player C says not the case that at most 1 of A,B,C,E,F are spies; since only one spy, C must be the spy (can lie or tell truth). Player D says B and C don't have the same role; B is knave, C is spy, so D tells truth, knight. E says not A is knight; A is knave, so E tells truth, knight. F says at most 2 of C,D,E,F are knights; D,E,F are knights, 3 knights, so F lies, knave or spy but spy taken by C, so F is knight. A's statement is false, so A is knave.

Player A says (at least 2 of A/B are knaves OR A/B same role). If A is knight, they share a role, so A is knight. Player B says there are 0 spies among A/F, which is false (F is spy), so B is knave. Player E claims A is not a knight, which is false, so E is knave. Player D says B and C have different roles; since B is knave, C must be knight to make D true, but C says there are >1 spies, which is false. Thus, C is knave, D is knight, and F is spy.
